summary: German broadcast criticism, Spanish scholarship and three independently authored Brazilian readings add disagreement and explain mechanisms of canonical visibility. Rosa receives affirmative and strongly dissenting readings, not three identical votes.
next: Add Asian/Arabic literary perspectives, then broaden philosophy beyond reference works.

sources.title: Ein düsteres Kapitel im Kanon der Weltliteratur
sources.note: Moritz emphasizes Hardy’s attack on marriage as an institution and the hostile reception that followed, alongside the novel’s realism.
sources.limits: New translation discussed separately from the underlying novel.

sources.title: Große Romane der Weltliteratur: Die Geschichte eines faszinierenden Genres
sources.note: Kesting uses Rabelais’s miniature world to trace the novel’s formal self-awareness and connects grotesque invention across centuries to Grass.
sources.limits: European-focused selection of forty works; interview is one source, not forty.

sources.title: Fest des Erzählens – Festival des Kommentierens
sources.note: Review highlights Mann’s expansion of marginalized biblical characters and commentary that complicates received claims about Freud’s influence and exposes speculative source material.
sources.limits: Novel’s borrowed pseudoscientific ideas are identified, not endorsed; commentary and novel distinguished.

sources.title: Resenha: Grande Sertão Veredas – Viver é muito perigoso!
sources.note: Rocha recalls overcoming repeated false starts as Rosa’s language evoked family speech; praises psychological chronology and philosophical reflection integrated with action.
sources.location: Personal reading history and narrative-technique paragraphs
sources.limits: Regional familiarity shapes this enthusiastic response.

targets.L: Local speech, narrative rhythm and accessibility.

sources.title: Grande Sertão: Veredas — uma resenha crítica
sources.note: Korytowski challenges reverence surrounding Rosa, questions the aimlessness of jagunço warfare and objects to romanticizing a violent narrator despite acknowledged poetic qualities.
sources.limits: Strongly moralizing counter-reading; character wrongdoing does not itself disprove literary achievement.

sources.title: 10 Considerações sobre Grande sertão: veredas
sources.note: Eralldo’s rereading foregrounds unresolved desire, religious doubt and the reader’s willingness to enter experimental narration, with attention to edition history.
sources.limits: Cited critical essays are not separately consulted; review contains plot disclosures.

sources.title: Clarín: las contradicciones de un realismo límite
sources.note: Traces Clarín’s move from naturalist totality toward psychological and poetic fiction, locating Su único hijo between extreme interiority and the grotesque.
sources.location: Novel-theory crisis and Su único hijo sections
sources.limits: One chapter of a larger study; cited critics are mediated evidence.

targets.A: Spanish fiction beyond a single canonical title.

sources.title: La presencia de Leopoldo Alas, La Estafeta Literaria
sources.note: Ballesteros shows that one influential magazine’s scant attention to Clarín failed to track his wider scholarly revival, revealing selective postwar visibility.
sources.location: Opening historical comparison and first publication period
sources.limits: Single periodical is an unrepresentative proxy; no absence-as-low-quality inference.
